response.reason: Four numbered NL segments were parsed for independently violable obligations. NL1 is purely descriptive scope-setting context. NL2 yields a continuous state_action obligation (target search performed continuously before mission completion) and a cardinality obligation over three state areas (ambiguous between concurrent_regions and direct_child_states, preserved with alternative_reading). NL3 yields a transition_endpoints obligation from the swarm's search/operating scope to the formation adjustment state, triggered by interception (event preserved via transition_groups). NL4 yields two further transition/effect obligations: a task-assignment-triggered transition to the attack state, and a decrease in UAV swarm count as a variable_delta effect that follows completion of the attack (with attack framed as completion of that state's activity, not a full termination of the whole system). No containment, initial-entry, or region-structure contract is manufactured beyond what NL explicitly supports; the exact source of the interception/task-assignment transitions is the ongoing "target search" operating scope established in NL2, continued via coreference ("it") in NL3 and NL4. Schema-correction repair: added the required per-group reason and basis fields to both transition_groups entries while preserving every prior valid contract and group content unchanged.

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, termination stability, and cross-wrapper reachability. Key findings: (1) NL-CONTRACT-REF-006 (initial_entry, owner=UAV swarm root -> target search scope) is satisfied at the root level ([*] -> SearchMission via Start_Mission at line 61), but that exact edge is unreachable from the top-level initial entry per inspection diagnostics (EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE / event-consumer:Start_Mission refuted), meaning the operating scope the NL requires the swarm to first enter is never actually entered by any reachable execution -- this is a root reachability defect on the owner entry obligation. (2) NL-CONTRACT-REF-002 cardinality: bound exactly once per protocol (three-region reading: Region1/Region2/Region3 nested composites under SearchMission). (3) Endpoint contracts REF-003/REF-004 (SearchMission->FormationAdjust, SearchMission->AttackState) are structurally present as SearchMission-scope transitions (line 57, line 59) and reachable per inspection reachable_from_initial=true, so they are satisfied at the transition level, but the deeper defect is that the entire SearchMission scope itself is not reachable from a genuine top-level initial entry (since the sole declared root->SearchMission edge, transition:line:61, is unreachable). This makes the whole SearchMission (and thus all descendant Search/FormationAdjust/AttackState behavior) unreachable from root, which is the true root-reachability defect -- distinct from and deeper than the owner initial_entry contract, and distinct from the individual endpoint contracts (which describe internal SearchMission-scope edges, not root entry). (4) Event consumer coverage for Interception_Detected and Task_Assignment_Received (REF-008/REF-009) show reachable consumer state refs are Search/InvalidFinaltr_0008/Region3/InvalidInitialtr_0005/InvalidInitialtr_0007 per inspection facts -- but these are all internal to SearchMission's descendant regions, which per finding (3) is itself unreachable from a genuine top-level initial entry, so reachable_consumer_transition_refs marked true in isolated inspection_equivalent_facts do not establish true root-reachable consumption; however per the routing discipline I must not double-count: the root-unreachability is the primary distinct defect, and event consumer coverage should be assessed as a separate derived contract only if a distinct scope defect exists beyond the root issue. I derive one additional_contracts row for root reachability of SearchMission specifically, and preserve REF-008/REF-009 event_consumption as satisfied at the local-consumer level (declared and locally reachable per the graph before considering root defect), omitting them to avoid duplicating the same root-unreachable defect twice. (5) Termination: SearchMission.Region1.Search transitions to a synthetic InvalidFinaltr_0008 (not a genuine final state) on Finished_Region3_Search, and per canonical IR the intended final was "@final:SearchMission.Region1.Region2.Region3"; however no NL contract in this supplied set addresses that as a termination_state, so no candidate is emitted for it under this round's supplied contracts. (6) NL-CONTRACT-REF-005 (variable_delta, attack effect must decrease UAV count) -- the only effect on Attacking's outgoing transition (line 55) is 'R45RouteToken = 14', a route-control variable, not a UAV-count decrement; there is no closed-model variable representing 'number of UAVs in the swarm' — this is a wrong_effect/missing semantic defect, preserved as predicate-null W1 since S5 covers guards not effects and variable_delta has no frozen predicate.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, termination stability, and cross-wrapper reachability. Key findings: (1) NL-CONTRACT-REF-006 (initial_entry, owner=UAV swarm root -> target search scope) is satisfied at the root level ([*] -> SearchMission via Start_Mission at line 61), but that exact edge is unreachable from the top-level initial entry per inspection diagnostics (EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE / event-consumer:Start_Mission refuted), meaning the operating scope the NL requires the swarm to first enter is never actually entered by any reachable execution -- this is a root reachability defect on the owner entry obligation. (2) NL-CONTRACT-REF-002 cardinality: bound exactly once per protocol (three-region reading: Region1/Region2/Region3 nested composites under SearchMission). (3) Endpoint contracts REF-003/REF-004 (SearchMission->FormationAdjust, SearchMission->AttackState) are structurally present as SearchMission-scope transitions (line 57, line 59) and reachable per inspection reachable_from_initial=true, so they are satisfied at the transition level, but the deeper defect is that the entire SearchMission scope itself is not reachable from a genuine top-level initial entry (since the sole declared root->SearchMission edge, transition:line:61, is unreachable). This makes the whole SearchMission (and thus all descendant Search/FormationAdjust/AttackState behavior) unreachable from root, which is the true root-reachability defect -- distinct from and deeper than the owner initial_entry contract, and distinct from the individual endpoint contracts (which describe internal SearchMission-scope edges, not root entry). (4) Event consumer coverage for Interception_Detected and Task_Assignment_Received (REF-008/REF-009) show reachable consumer state refs are Search/InvalidFinaltr_0008/Region3/InvalidInitialtr_0005/InvalidInitialtr_0007 per inspection facts -- but these are all internal to SearchMission's descendant regions, which per finding (3) is itself unreachable from a genuine top-level initial entry, so reachable_consumer_transition_refs marked true in isolated inspection_equivalent_facts do not establish true root-reachable consumption; however per the routing discipline I must not double-count: the root-unreachability is the primary distinct defect, and event consumer coverage should be assessed as a separate derived contract only if a distinct scope defect exists beyond the root issue. I derive one additional_contracts row for root reachability of SearchMission specifically, and preserve REF-008/REF-009 event_consumption as satisfied at the local-consumer level (declared and locally reachable per the graph before considering root defect), omitting them to avoid duplicating the same root-unreachable defect twice. (5) Termination: SearchMission.Region1.Search transitions to a synthetic InvalidFinaltr_0008 (not a genuine final state) on Finished_Region3_Search, and per canonical IR the intended final was "@final:SearchMission.Region1.Region2.Region3"; however no NL contract in this supplied set addresses that as a termination_state, so no candidate is emitted for it under this round's supplied contracts. (6) NL-CONTRACT-REF-005 (variable_delta, attack effect must decrease UAV count) -- the only effect on Attacking's outgoing transition (line 55) is 'R45RouteToken = 14', a route-control variable, not a UAV-count decrement; there is no closed-model variable representing 'number of UAVs in the swarm' — this is a wrong_effect/missing semantic defect, preserved as predicate-null W1 since S5 covers guards not effects and variable_delta has no frozen predicate.

stage_receipts.reason: Four numbered NL segments were parsed for independently violable obligations. NL1 is purely descriptive scope-setting context. NL2 yields a continuous state_action obligation (target search performed continuously before mission completion) and a cardinality obligation over three state areas (ambiguous between concurrent_regions and direct_child_states, preserved with alternative_reading). NL3 yields a transition_endpoints obligation from the swarm's search/operating scope to the formation adjustment state, triggered by interception (event preserved via transition_groups). NL4 yields two further transition/effect obligations: a task-assignment-triggered transition to the attack state, and a decrease in UAV swarm count as a variable_delta effect that follows completion of the attack (with attack framed as completion of that state's activity, not a full termination of the whole system). No containment, initial-entry, or region-structure contract is manufactured beyond what NL explicitly supports; the exact source of the interception/task-assignment transitions is the ongoing "target search" operating scope established in NL2, continued via coreference ("it") in NL3 and NL4.
